Android from the foundation · Puzzle 8 of 15

What's inside the APK

Phones have different CPUs, but you ship one APK. So the APK can't hold instructions for one CPU, and something on the phone has to run them.

The problem

You upload one APK, and it runs on phones with very different CPUs. But a CPU only runs instructions written for that kind of CPU. So what's in the APK, and who makes it run?

See it

Save this diagram as a GIF

The building block

Each kind of CPU has its own language: machine code. Your APK doesn't contain it. Your Kotlin compiles to DEX, compact instructions written for Android, not for any one CPU.

On the phone, ART, the Android Runtime (the part that runs your code), works inside your app's process and makes the DEX run. The simplest way it does that is interpreting: reading one DEX instruction at a time and doing what it says. That always works, but it's slow.

The analogy

You write your recipes in one common language, so any kitchen can use them. In every house lives a translator, ART, who reads them to the cook word by word.

Check yourself

You ship the same APK to two phones with different CPUs. Why does it run on both?

Not quite. Nobody rebuilds it: ART on the phone runs the same DEX.

Not quite. Then it would only run on the CPUs it was built for. DEX isn't for any CPU.

Right. DEX isn't tied to a CPU; ART on each phone runs it.

Is there one ART for all the apps on the phone?

Not quite. ART lives inside each app's process, like a translator in every house.

Right. Each process has its own ART.

What's the difference between DEX and machine code?

Right. DEX needs ART; machine code needs nothing.

Not quite. DEX has to be run by ART; machine code runs on the CPU directly.

What you now know

Your Kotlin compiles to DEX, which no CPU runs directly. ART, inside your app's process, runs it: at first by reading it one instruction at a time.
